newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to begin second term with high popularity.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to begin second term with high popularity.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will begin his second term with a high approval rating despite recent publicity on sexual harrassment allegations against him and a campaign finance scandal, according to a new poll.
The poll released on Wednesday by the Pew Research Centre showed Clinton with a 59 percent approval rating, the highest ever recorded by this particular survey.

Pollster Andrew Kohunt said Clinton was enjoying a second honeymoon with voters fairly typical for second term presidents. His standing was comparable to President Ronald Reagan's at the time of his second inauguration in 1985.
Favourable opinion of Congress was also up sharply to 56 percent, but House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich had a 65 percent unfavourable rating.
Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright had a 57 percent favourable score, with men and women rating her equally and Republicans as well as Democrats giving her high marks.
Asked what were the top issues facing the nation's leaders, Republicans and Democrats agreed that fixing Social Security was the No. 1 priority.
